nodes.name: audio_speech
nodes.description: Pure audio preprocessing, spectral feature, alignment, and CTC decoding atoms.
nodes.conceptual_summary: Audio and speech primitives decomposed from the 05 research bundle.
nodes.decomposition_rationale: Each atom is a pure function boundary with explicit array inputs and no file I/O or model state.

nodes.name: resample_audio
nodes.description: Resample audio along the sample axis using polyphase anti-alias filtering.
nodes.type_signature: (signal: NDArray[np.float64], orig_sr: int, target_sr: int) -> NDArray[np.float64]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Reduces sample-rate ratios and applies scipy polyphase resampling.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: scipy.signal.resample_poly designs an FIR filter of length proportional to max(up, down) and uses polyphase decomposition via upfirdn to resample the signal of length n, taking O(n * max(up, down)) time. The space complexity is O(n * (up / down)) to store the output signal plus O(max(up, down)) for the filter coefficients. (derived from analyzing the actual function scipy.signal.resample_poly rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.conceptual_summary: Creates a frame-by-sample view and locks writes to preserve purity.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: numpy.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view constructs a new strided array view pointing to the same memory block by updating metadata strides, requiring constant O(1) time and O(1) space. (derived from analyzing the actual function numpy.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.complexity_reasoning: numpy.fft.rfft computes the 1D real Fast Fourier Transform along the window axis of size w for all f frames, taking O(f * w * log(w)) time and O(f * w) space to allocate the resulting spectral magnitude arrays. (derived from analyzing the actual function numpy.fft.rfft rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.complexity_reasoning: scipy.fft.dct computes the 1-D Discrete Cosine Transform (type II) of size m along the frequency axis for each of the f frames, running in O(f * m * log(m)) time via FFT-based algorithms and requiring O(m * f) space for the output cepstral coefficients. (derived from analyzing the actual function scipy.fft.dct rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: ebu_r128_normalize
nodes.description: Normalize 48 kHz audio using K-weighted gated loudness.
nodes.type_signature: (signal: NDArray[np.float64], sr: int, target_lufs: float) -> NDArray[np.float64]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Applies fixed 48 kHz K-weighting filters, absolute gate, relative gate, and gain scaling.
nodes.critic_notes: The atom intentionally requires sr == 48000 because the research provided fixed 48 kHz coefficients.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: ITU-R BS.1770 48 kHz coefficients normalization filters a signal of length n using low-order IIR filters (linear time O(n)) and computes gated integrated loudness in overlapping fixed-length blocks (overall O(n) operations), requiring O(n) space to allocate the filtered arrays and normalized output. (derived from analyzing the actual function ITU-R BS.1770 48 kHz coefficients rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: rule_based_g2p
nodes.description: Convert text to phoneme IDs using explicit regex context rules.
nodes.type_signature: (text: str, ruleset: dict[str, tuple[int, str, str]]) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Runs longest-match grapheme rules with explicit left and right regex context.
nodes.critic_notes: The caller owns language-specific rules; unmatched characters map to code points.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: rule-based G2P converts text of length n using a ruleset of size r, matching graphemes and performing regular expression searches on left and right contexts of length up to n, taking worst-case O(r * n^2) time and requiring O(n) space to store the sliced strings and the output phonemes. (derived from analyzing the actual function rule-based G2P rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: dtw_alignment
nodes.description: Find a monotonic frame-to-token DTW path from frame probabilities.
nodes.conceptual_summary: Uses a stay-or-advance dynamic program over target-token likelihoods.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: dynamic time warping uses dynamic programming to align f frames and t phoneme tokens, filling a cost and backpointer grid of shape f x t in O(f * t) time and requiring O(f * t) space. (derived from analyzing the actual function dynamic time warping rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: monotonic_alignment_search
nodes.description: Compute a hard monotonic maximum-score path for each batch item.
nodes.type_signature: (value: NDArray[np.float64], mask: NDArray[np.float64], max_neg_val: float) -> NDArray[np.float64]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Maximizes a monotonic score path through token-by-frame tensors.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: monotonic alignment search implements dynamic programming to compute maximum score alignment paths for a batch of size b, with t tokens and f frames, running in O(b * t * f) time and requiring O(b * t * f) space to store the DP and alignment grids. (derived from analyzing the actual function monotonic alignment search rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: ctc_greedy_decode
nodes.description: Collapse the highest-probability CTC path into token IDs.
nodes.conceptual_summary: Argmaxes frames, removes repeated labels, and drops blanks.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: CTC greedy decoding finds the maximum probability token per frame from a log probability array of shape f x v (where f is frames and v is vocabulary size) taking O(f * v) time, and collapses duplicates in linear O(f) time, requiring O(f) space for the decoded sequence. (derived from analyzing the actual function CTC greedy decoding rather than the opaque wrapper)

nodes.name: ctc_beam_decode
nodes.description: Decode CTC log probabilities with prefix beam search.
nodes.type_signature: (log_probs: NDArray[np.float64], beam_width: int, blank_id: int, alpha: float, beta: float) -> list[tuple[list[int], float]]
nodes.conceptual_summary: Tracks blank and non-blank prefix scores separately and prunes by total log score.
nodes.critic_notes: No language model object is accepted, so alpha is reserved and beta acts as insertion bonus.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: CTC prefix beam search processes f frames with beam width B and vocabulary size v. In each step, it expands all active prefixes and sorts the top candidates, taking O(f * B * v * log(B * v)) time and requiring O(B * v) space to hold the beam state. (derived from analyzing the actual function CTC prefix beam search rather than the opaque wrapper)
